svg.text: Level 3 — Twelve Failures, and Not One of Them Raises an Error
Level 2's failures were wrong answers. Level 3's are correct systems doing exactly what they were told.
CHAPTER
WHAT GOES WRONG — with every signal green
THE ONE SIGNAL THAT SEES IT

g.text: 21 Durable execution
A debugging replay re-runs every effect; three duplicate PRs
activity identity, checked before the call
22 Event spine
One malformed row; a cursor correctly declines to advance; everything stops
age of the oldest unclaimed event
23 Scheduler
One tenant's 400 runs stop everyone else for two hours, at full throughput
queue time per latency class, per tenant
24 Task graph
A join counts a branch that never committed — or misses one that did
age of the oldest non-terminal node
25 World model
The run's own refactor invalidates its map; the next edit lands on dead code
belief.contradicted, per probe
26 Planning algorithms
Six identical replans from unchanged inputs; it looks like diligence
plans per goal; replan.refused
27 Failure and rollback
A clean rollback reverts every commit and leaves the migration on staging
age of the oldest outstanding obligation
28 Grading
A skipped test is a green suite; the grader agrees, correctly, with itself
false-pass rate against the golden set
29 Long-running agents
190 steps oscillating between two states; the step counter rises steadily
novel durable state, over effectful steps
30 Human authority
Eleven weeks of compliance with a prompt rule, then one loss
gated-effect coverage — it must be 1.0
31 Safety and sandboxing
A pasted log line becomes a plan step; exfiltration has no symptom at all
egress.blocked — silence is the alarm
32 Distributed execution
A paused worker wakes and finishes a deploy someone else already did
longest effect duration vs lease TTL

svg.text: Three shapes recur, and each was arrived at independently more than once
Replace a position with a question
Ch 17 lock → version compared on write
Ch 22 cursor → per-event claim
Ch 24 step index → ready-set query
A remembered position has crash semantics.
A question over durable rows has none.
Permit one direction only
Ch 28 judgment may lower, never raise
Ch 31 provenance falls, never rises
Ch 30 a gate holds, never starts
Forbid the direction the bias — or the
adversary — would push, and it goes inert.
Enforce in the signature
Ch 26 repair() cannot receive the goal
Ch 28 Judge() cannot receive reasoning
Ch 31 capability cannot receive content
When a rule matters more than anyone will
remember it, remove the data to break it.
One boolean from Chapter 14 — pure or effectful — turned out to answer four unrelated questions nobody asked it
Ch 14 does this need a gate? · Ch 24 may this branch be raced? · Ch 25 does this invalidate a belief? · Ch 30 which tier gates, and where?
A distinction that keeps answering questions it was not cut for is usually a real seam — which is why Ch 20 §5.5 puts it outside the evolvable workspace.
